title: Code Viewer reads single-byte files only in the system code page (no CP852 etc.)
problem: The Code Viewer (codeview plug-in, the default for F3 on source and text files) decodes a file without a BOM that is not UTF-8 with `CP_ACP` only. The product's conversion tables - the `EnumConversionTables` machinery the built-in viewer uses for ISO-8859-2, CP852, Kamenicky, KOI-8 and the others - are not wired in, and the F8 encoding menu is a fixed list of five encodings. A single-byte file in another code page than the system's (e.g. a DOS CP852 or an ISO-8859-2 text on a CP1250 machine) therefore shows wrong letters, and the user cannot choose the right table in the Code Viewer; the workaround is the built-in viewer. The 070 stabilization review called it "the single largest remaining gap against the spec" (FR-024).
evidence: specs/070-source-viewer-plugin/stabilization-review.md: finding F16 (table row ~L62: "The ANSI decode path is hardwired to `CP_ACP`; the code-table machinery FR-024 calls for (ISO-8859-2, CP852, ...) is absent"), section 4 ("F16 (code tables). Not fixed") and section 7 *Deferred, with reasons*. Spec: specs/070-source-viewer-plugin/spec.md FR-024 (~L523). Site at 7993914c: src/plugins/codeview/intake.cpp ~624-631 (`// --- encoding (spec FR-024) ---`, `UINT codePage = CP_ACP;`). Recorded in specs/070-source-viewer-plugin/REMAINING-WORK.md, header *Update 2026-08-27 (third round)* ("Two things it did NOT cover remain open: ... the code-table gap (FR-024), now recorded as F16"); not in specs/NEXT-WORK.md at 7993914c.
expected: The Code Viewer can decode a single-byte file with any conversion table the built-in viewer offers; its encoding menu lists them, the choice is applied to the open file and remembered as the built-in viewer's is; files that decode correctly today (UTF-8, UTF-16, the system code page) are unchanged.
approach: From the stabilization review section 7: a feature-sized piece of work with its own UI question (how the table list is presented and remembered). Feature 069 established that the table names reach plug-ins as code-page bytes (`CCodeTablesData::Name`, handed out by `EnumConversionTables` and accepted back by `GetConversionTable`; dbviewer and filecomp persist them - RW069 section 1, B-5), and the plug-in's UTF-8 pipeline must respect that. Doing it badly would break the encoding menu that works today.
notes: Area: the Code Viewer is a plug-in (other-plugins); its core-side viewer machinery is the built-in viewer's. Related to encoding cluster B-5 (frozen plug-in-facing services), which another part of the migration takes from specs/NEXT-WORK.md section A.19.
log: 070 stabilization review: F16 deferred - a feature, not a repair

title: Code Viewer: its known limitations are not stated anywhere a user can read
problem: Feature 070's handoff listed three limitations of the Code Viewer "to state in the changelog when this ships": (1) 18 grammars and 1 theme are excluded for licence reasons, so `.glsl`, `.matlab`, `.tcl`, nginx configs, Ada, gnuplot, Racket and org files open as plain text (`glsl` additionally ships as a minimal no-op grammar stub because C++, Elm and Nim declare it in `embeddedLangs`); (2) the plain band (over 1 MB, or lines over 20,000 characters) has no highlighting by design; (3) "Restore default file types" takes effect at the next application start, because the viewer list can only be written from `Connect()`. The plug-in shipped in 0.1.6 (build 190) without them: the 0.1.6 entry of CHANGELOG.md does not mention them and no user-facing document does (a search for `glsl` finds only specs/070-*).
evidence: specs/070-source-viewer-plugin/REMAINING-WORK.md, *Known limitations to state in the changelog when this ships* (L167-178); fix-log.md defect 1 (the glsl stub). CHANGELOG.md `## [0.1.6] - 2026-08-29` (L1896-1930 at 7993914c) has no such text. Not in specs/NEXT-WORK.md at 7993914c.
expected: The three limitations are stated in a user-facing place - the Code Viewer's page of the manual once a manual ships, or the README / the next release notes - with the excluded-format list re-checked against the plug-in's current data.
notes: Re-check the list of excluded grammars before stating it (src/plugins/codeview/test, `gen_langmap.py`, the licence exclusions in the 070 research) - it may have changed since 2026-08-26. Where the text goes depends on the decision about shipping a manual (help-contents-fails-no-manual-shipped).

title: File Comparator stores an uninitialised byte in its saved configuration
problem: Byte 77 of the File Comparator's 92-byte `Configuration` registry blob differs between any two runs (`02` / `01`) with unchanged settings. Harmless for the comparison, but configuration exports differ for no reason (and an uninitialised byte is read from the stack or heap).
evidence: specs/080-restart-manager-upgrade/REMAINING-WORK.md, *Found on the way, not part of this feature* (L105-109): "Likely padding after `unsigned char WhiteSpace` in `src/plugins/filecomp/dlg_com.h`". At 7993914c `struct CRegBLOBConfiguration` (`dlg_com.h` ~L152-165, "as stored in binary form in registry. DO NOT MODIFY") has `BOOL`, `int`, `int`, `LOGFONT` (60 bytes), `BOOL`, then `unsigned char WhiteSpace` at offset 76 followed by the 4-byte `CFileViewMode ViewMode` - bytes 77-79 are padding, which matches byte 77. Not in specs/NEXT-WORK.md at 7993914c.
expected: Two runs with the same settings store byte-identical `Configuration` blobs (the structure is zero-initialised before it is filled, or the padding is made explicit), and older stored blobs still load.
notes: Possibly done - verify: no later feature records a fix, but the blob was not compared again at HEAD. Measure first (export the key twice across two runs, compare).

title: Should the program come back after a reboot or sign-in (RESTART_NO_REBOOT)?
problem: Feature 080 registers the program for a restart after an installer's update (`RegisterApplicationRestart`) but excludes the restart after a reboot or sign-out with `RESTART_NO_REBOOT` (080 spec, *Assumptions*). Removing the flag is a one-word change and a product decision.
evidence: specs/080-restart-manager-upgrade/REMAINING-WORK.md section P4 (L96-101). At 7993914c: src/mainwnd3.cpp:619 `RegisterApplicationRestart(cmdLine, RESTART_NO_CRASH | RESTART_NO_HANG | RESTART_NO_REBOOT)`. Not in specs/NEXT-WORK.md at 7993914c.
notes: Verifying option B needs a real reboot and a sign-out with Windows' "restart apps after signing in" enabled - a person step.
question: Should Tandem Commander reappear after a reboot or at sign-in for users who enabled Windows' "restart apps after signing in", like other registered programs?
options:
- A - keep `RESTART_NO_REBOOT` (today): the restart registration serves updates only; nothing reappears at sign-in.
- B - remove the flag: the program comes back after a reboot / sign-in when the user enabled the Windows option; costs: unrelated to updates, makes the program reappear at sign-in, can be verified only with a real reboot.
recommendation: A - the 080 spec's assumption; revisit only if users ask for it.

title: Help > Contents ends in a Help Error box: the product ships no manual
problem: The shipped product contains no help files: `help\` is not in the Release tree or the installer, so *Help > Contents* (also the toolbar's help button and the Find window's help command, `CM_HELP_CONTENTS`) ends in a *Help Error* box, in every release. The manual's sources exist (`help/src`, an HTML Help project `salamand.hhp`) but are not rebranded - 236 of 237 pages still carry the 2023 Open Salamander footer.
evidence: specs/080-restart-manager-upgrade/REMAINING-WORK.md, *Found on the way, not part of this feature* (L110-112): "*Help -> Contents* ends in a *Help Error* box. Known in spirit (the help is not rebranded yet), but worth stating plainly." At 7993914c: setup/tandemcommander.iss has no help entry; `CM_HELP_CONTENTS` handled in src/mainwnd3.cpp ~2987 and src/finddlg1.cpp ~3946, toolbar button src/toolbar4.cpp:204. Not in specs/NEXT-WORK.md at 7993914c (only the footers, *Recorded, deliberately not on the list*).
notes: Context-sensitive F1 in dialogs was not checked. The footer entry is migrated by another part (item help-pages-carry-2023-open-salamander-footer, from NEXT-WORK *Recorded, deliberately not on the list*).
question: What should the Help commands do while the product ships no manual?
options:
- A - build the manual from `help/src` as it is and ship it with the installer (Open Salamander text and footers included).
- B - rebrand the manual first (a feature series), then ship it.
- C - until a manual ships, make the Help commands say plainly that no manual is installed (or open the project's website) instead of the Help Error box.
recommendation: C now (removes the error box at little cost; a website link would be new network-facing behaviour - PRIVACY.md), B when a manual is wanted. A suggestion of the migration, not decided.

title: Closing for an update: four limitations accepted by feature 080
reason: Accepted as known limitations by feature 080 (REMAINING-WORK.md P3, 2026-09-20): each needs an extreme case (a plug-in `Release()` hanging for half a minute), is what a forced close asks for, concerns only the first update from 0.1.7, or is the single `WM_CLOSE` the Restart Manager itself sends. Re-open only with a new reason.
problem: (1) An execute stage that outlives the requester's 30 s is not stopped: the installer reports failure while the program still closes, and nothing starts it again (measured closes take 1.2-1.4 s; a plug-in whose `Release()` hangs for half a minute would be needed). (2) A forced close (`/FORCECLOSEAPPLICATIONS`) of a program that declined ends in the Restart Manager killing it after 30 s - without saving the configuration (before 080 the same situation also showed a *forced shutdown* box). (3) The first update from 0.1.7 does not bring the program back: the restart registration lives in the old process and 0.1.7 never registered (moot for updates from 0.1.8 on). (4) One genuine `WM_CLOSE` within 35 s after an installer's instruction is ignored (the Restart Manager sends one of its own, which must not start the interactive exit); a second Alt+F4 works.
evidence: specs/080-restart-manager-upgrade/REMAINING-WORK.md section P3 *Known limitations, accepted* (L80-94); closing record specs/080-restart-manager-upgrade/closing-report.md. Not in specs/NEXT-WORK.md at 7993914c.
notes: Related decided entries of other parts: specs/NEXT-WORK.md section C "Update close" (declining windows kept, 118/121).
log: feature 080: the four limitations accepted (REMAINING-WORK P3)
